course_name_original: Teoría de estructuras y construcciones industriales
course_name_en: Theory of Structures and Industrial Constructions
prerequisites: Elasticidad y ampliación de resistencia de materiales/V12G380V01502

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the requirements that structures must meet to fulfill their functions, considering acting forces, safety criteria, and calculation bases.
learning_outcomes.code: B3 B4 B5 B6 B11 C23 D2 D5 D8 D9 D10 D17

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the ability to convert a real structure into a model for its analysis, and vice versa.
learning_outcomes.code: B3 B4 B5 B6 B11 C23 D2 D5 D8 D9 D10 D17

learning_outcomes.text: Identify the most important typologies and elements used in structures and industrial constructions.
learning_outcomes.code: B3 B4 B5 B6 B11 C23 D2 D5 D8 D9 D10 D17

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the conditions that govern the behavior of structures in their different typologies.
learning_outcomes.code: B3 B4 B5 B6 B11 C23 D2 D5 D8 D9 D10 D17

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to determine stress laws, stresses, and deformations in structural elements.
learning_outcomes.code: B3 B4 B5 B6 B11 C23 D2 D5 D8 D9 D10 D17

syllabus_topics: Introduction: General principles
Introduction: Structural typologies
Introduction: Types of structural analysis
Actions: Regulations
Actions: Determination of actions
Structural safety: Generalities
Structural safety: Concept of limit state - Ultimate limit states - Serviceability limit states
Structural safety: Probabilistic method for structural analysis. Structural reliability.
Structural safety: Semi-probabilistic method for structural analysis. Partial safety factors
Structural safety: Combination of actions
Structural typologies and industrial constructions: Description of the main structural typologies and construction elements used (Steel, Concrete, Wood)
Structural typologies and industrial constructions: Deconstructibility and eco-sustainable structures (Reusable and Reconfigurable)
Reticular structures with articulated nodes: Degree of hyperstaticity. Criticality.
Reticular structures with articulated nodes: Isostatic systems. Calculation methods
Reticular structures with articulated nodes: Hyperstatic systems. Calculation methods
Reticular structures with rigid nodes: Definitions
Reticular structures with rigid nodes: Order of translationality
Reticular structures with rigid nodes: Calculation using the Cross method
Matrix calculation of structures: Definitions
Matrix calculation of structures: Stiffness matrix. Local and global coordinates.
Matrix calculation of structures: Assembly of the stiffness matrix
Matrix calculation of structures: Matrix calculation of structures
Structural calculation using finite elements: Introduction to the method
Structural calculation using finite elements: Formulation
Structural calculation using finite elements: Preprocessing. Calculation. Postprocessing.
Structural calculation using finite elements: Calibration of numerical models based on experimental data
assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must obtain a minimum of 40% of the maximum grade in the development questions exam, which is reduced to 35% for students attending at least 80% of theoretical classes. Similarly, a minimum of 40% (35% with 80% attendance) is required from the sum of objective questions exams. Students officially waiving continuous assessment will have their grade based 100% on the final exam. In the July exam, the final exam and objective questions exam grades can be recovered, but project, problem sheets, and practical grades are not recoverable. Unethical behavior (copying, plagiarism, unauthorized electronic devices) will result in a failing grade of 0.0 for the course.
